<a id="savebackupcontent"></a>

## `SaveBackupContent`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Backups.SaveBackupContent` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

File work for the launch save backups, Unity-free: hashing a folder, copying it, and removing an old backup safely. Used by [`SaveBackupRunner`](#savebackuprunner); exercised against temp folders by the tests.

**Content hash.** SHA-256 over every regular file under the folder, in ordinal order of the relative path written with `/` separators. Each file contributes: the UTF-8 bytes of its relative path, one `0x00` byte, its length as 8 bytes little-endian, then its bytes. The separator and the length make the encoding unambiguous, so a rename, a move between folders or a byte moved from one file to the next all change the hash. Empty folders do not count. The hash is lowercase hex.

**Links.** A symbolic link or junction (`FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`) is never followed, copied or hashed - it is listed in [`SaveBackupContentSummary.SkippedLinks`](#savebackupcontentsummary--skippedlinks). A backup folder that contains one is never deleted ([`SaveBackupContent.TryDeleteBackupFolder`](#savebackupcontent--trydeletebackupfolder)), so a delete can never reach outside it.

<a id="savebackupcontent--copytree"></a>

### `static SaveBackupContentSummary CopyTree(string source, string destination)`

Copies `source` into the new folder `destination` (which must not exist yet): every folder and regular file, each file's bytes and last-write time. Each file is read once; the bytes written are the bytes hashed, so the returned hash describes the copy exactly.

Files are not forced to disk one by one (`Flush(true)`): measured at about 5 ms per file on macOS, 230 ms for a 46-file save, against 4 ms without. A crash of the game leaves the written data with the operating system either way; only a power cut or an OS crash in the first seconds after a launch could lose it.

**Parameters**

- `source`: The folder to copy.
- `destination`: Where the copy goes; created here.

**Exceptions**

- `IOException`: `destination` already exists, or a file cannot be read or written.

<a id="savebackupcontent--measure"></a>

### `static SaveBackupContentSummary Measure(string folder)`

Counts and hashes the files under `folder`. Reads every file once.

**Parameters**

- `folder`: An existing folder.

<a id="savebackupcontent--trydeletebackupfolder"></a>

### `static bool TryDeleteBackupFolder(string folder, out string problem)`

Deletes one backup folder and everything in it - unless it contains a symbolic link or junction, in which case nothing is deleted. Read-only files are made writable first (Windows refuses to delete them).

**Parameters**

- `folder`: The backup folder. The caller has already checked that it is one of ours.
- `problem`: Why it was not (fully) deleted.

## `SaveBackupManifest`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Backups.SaveBackupManifest` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

`backup.json`, the marker in every launch save backup. A folder whose marker does not parse, or whose `kind` is not [`SaveBackupManifest.Kind`](#savebackupmanifest--kind), is not one of ours and is never deleted.

```csharp
{
  "kind": "cwyls.save-backup",
  "schema": 1,
  "created": "2026-11-01T14:03:12.345+07:00",
  "loaderVersion": "0.9.0",
  "gameVersion": "1.18.0",
  "files": 46,
  "bytes": 188416,
  "contentSha256": "<64 lowercase hex digits>"
}
```

`contentSha256` is [`SaveBackupContent`](#savebackupcontent)'s hash of the `SaveData` folder in the backup.

<a id="savebackuppolicy"></a>

## `SaveBackupPolicy`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Backups.SaveBackupPolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which launch save backups to keep, with restic `forget` semantics. Pure.

The backups are walked newest first. Each rule has a budget ([`SaveBackupRules`](#savebackuprules)) and a "last period" it kept. A backup is kept by `last` while that budget lasts. It is kept by `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` when its period differs from the last period that rule kept and the rule still has budget; the rule then spends one and remembers the period. So each rule keeps the newest backup of each of its N most recent periods *that have a backup* (a week without a launch does not use up a daily slot). A backup is kept when any rule keeps it, and removed otherwise. This is the algorithm of restic's `ApplyPolicy` (`internal/restic/snapshot_policy.go`) for `--keep-last/-daily/-weekly/-monthly`.

Periods are taken from the local time in the folder name. A day is a local calendar day. A week is an ISO 8601 week (Monday to Sunday; week 1 is the week with the year's first Thursday, so 31 Dec can be in week 1 of the next year and 1 Jan in week 52 or 53 of the previous one) - restic uses ISO weeks too. A month is a calendar month.

Ties: backups with the same time are ordered by name, descending (ordinal). Names come from the time, so a tie only happens with duplicate input.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--lastreason"></a>

### `const string LastReason = "last"`

The reason given by `KeepLast`.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--apply"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<SaveBackupDecision> Apply(IEnumerable<SaveBackupStamp> backups, SaveBackupRules rules)`

Decides, for every backup, keep or remove, and why.

**Parameters**

- `backups`: The backups. Order does not matter; null is treated as empty.
- `rules`: The rules; null means [`SaveBackupRules.Default`](#savebackuprules--default).

**Returns:** One decision per backup, newest first.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--daykey"></a>

### `static string DayKey(DateTime time)`

The day period: `2026-10-31`.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--isoweek"></a>

### `static (int, int) IsoWeek(DateTime time)`

The ISO 8601 week-numbering year and week (1-53) of a date. Written out rather than taken from `System.Globalization.ISOWeek`, which the game's Mono profile is not guaranteed to have; the tests compare it with `ISOWeek` day by day.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--monthkey"></a>

### `static string MonthKey(DateTime time)`

The month period: `2026-10`.

<a id="savebackuppolicy--weekkey"></a>

<a id="savebackuprunner"></a>

## `SaveBackupRunner`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Backups.SaveBackupRunner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One launch save backup, Unity-free: hash the save, compare with the newest backup, copy it to a `.partial-` folder, verify, write the marker, rename, then prune by [`SaveBackupPolicy`](#savebackuppolicy). Never throws: every failure is a [`SaveBackupOutcome.Failed`](#savebackupoutcome--failed) result.

Safety rules, all enforced here:

- The backups folder may not be the save folder or inside it (Steam Cloud syncs the save folder), nor the other way round.
- A backup only gets its final name once its files, their verification and its marker are all written, so a crash never leaves a half backup that looks valid; a leftover `.partial-` folder is never mistaken for a backup.
- Pruning deletes only folders named `save-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` holding a valid `backup.json` (checked again right before the delete) and containing no links. Nothing else is ever deleted, except this run's own `.partial-` folder after a failure.
- Nothing is pruned when the new backup failed.

<a id="savebackuprunner--issameorinside"></a>

### `static bool IsSameOrInside(string path, string folder)`

True when `path` is `folder` or somewhere inside it. Compared on full paths, ignoring case (the cautious answer on case-insensitive macOS and Windows volumes).

<a id="savebackuprunner--prune"></a>

### `static SaveBackupPruneResult Prune(string backupsRoot, SaveBackupRules rules)`

Applies the rules to the backups folder and deletes what no rule keeps. Folders that are not ours are never touched. Never throws for a single folder; a delete that fails is reported in [`SaveBackupPruneResult.Problems`](#savebackuppruneresult--problems).

**Parameters**

- `backupsRoot`: The backups folder.
- `rules`: The rules.

<a id="savebackuprunner--run"></a>

### `static SaveBackupResult Run(SaveBackupRequest request)`

Runs one launch backup. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `request`: What to do.
